dayToDay.notes: Students are with their guide group essentially the entire trip, sleeping outdoors at shared backcountry campsites, with a staff-to-camper ratio of at least 2 staff per 10 youth. Days are highly structured: hiking, a daily morning meeting, evening group activities and a campfire, and shared meals prepared together. There's no cell service in the backcountry, so there's no phone or text contact with family during the trip — guides send a nightly satellite check-in to the office, not to parents, consistent with the program's "no news is good news" approach. Parents receive a recap email with photos and a daily journal about 1–2 weeks after the trip ends.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Lasting Adventures Yosemite summer camp FAQ pages (identical language across 6-Day Young Adventurer's, 6-Day High Country, and 10-Day Mammoth pages)

dayToDay.notes: Students are with their guide group essentially the entire trip, sleeping outdoors at shared backcountry campsites, with a staff-to-camper ratio of at least 2 staff per 10 youth. Days are highly structured: hiking, a daily morning meeting, evening group activities, and shared meals prepared together. There's no cell service in the backcountry, so there's no phone or text contact with family during the trip - guides send a nightly satellite check-in to the office, not to parents. Parents receive a recap email with photos and a daily journal about 1-2 weeks after the trip ends.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Lasting Adventures Olympic summer camp FAQ pages (identical language across all Olympic offering pages)

Days are highly structured: hiking, a daily morning meeting, evening group activities, and shared meals prepared together. There's no cell service in the backcountry, so there's no phone or text contact with family during the trip - guides send a nightly satellite check-in to the office, not to parents. Parents receive a recap email with photos and a daily journal about 1-2 weeks after the trip ends. This trip includes a round-trip shuttle from Fresno/Yosemite International Airport.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Lasting Adventures Sequoia summer camp FAQ page

dayToDay.notes: Rustic, traditional overnight camp centered on cabin-group living, with cabin community and staff role models framed as the core of the program. Tiered pricing lets families self-select an affordable tuition level without affecting the camper's experience - the tier chosen is kept confidential.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Camp Becket program pages and BCCYMCA Dates & Rates page (bccymca.org)

dayToDay.notes: Rustic, traditional overnight camp for girls and gender non-binary campers who prefer female housing, centered on cabin-group living. Tiered pricing lets families self-select an affordable tuition level without affecting the camper's experience - the tier chosen is kept confidential.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Chimney Corners program pages and BCCYMCA Dates & Rates page (bccymca.org)

dayToDay.notes: This is an island-based residential camp with structured cabin groups of about 8-10 campers per counselor; certified dive staff supervise at closer ratios (1 instructor per 4 campers for scuba certification, 1 per 8 for snorkeling). There is no phone contact between parents and campers at all during a session - the camp states this is an intentional independence policy, not just a logistics limitation. The only outbound communication is one-way: parents get 5 free email credits per camper per week (more purchasable), and campers can write letters, but there's no video call or phone option. In-session visits or tours from parents are not permitted. A registered nurse is on-site for the full summer.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Catalina Sea Camp 1-Week Programs page and Parent FAQs

dayToDay.notes: Students live in one of over 120 cabins across Interlochen's 1,200-acre campus, organized by division. Days combine classes, rehearsals, and coursework with time for swimming in one of two campus lakes, crafts, pickup sports, and other traditional camp activities. Programs longer than one week that require an audition or portfolio are automatically considered for merit scholarships; need-based financial aid is also available for any program longer than one week (one-week Intensives are not aid-eligible). Admission for all programs is submitted through Interlochen's Education Community portal, with a Jan. 15 priority deadline for the following summer.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Interlochen Arts Camp tuition/financial aid page and general camp materials (interlochen.org)

dayToDay.notes: Students live in one of over 120 cabins across Interlochen's 1,200-acre campus, grouped with other Intermediate-age campers. Alongside daily rehearsals/coursework in their chosen program, students have time for traditional camp activities - swimming, field games, and archery. Every program at this division runs 3 or 6 weeks and is eligible for need-based financial aid; programs longer than one week that require an audition or portfolio are automatically considered for merit scholarships. Admission is submitted through Interlochen's Education Community portal, with a Jan. 15 priority deadline for the following summer.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Interlochen grades 6-8 program pages and tuition/financial aid page (interlochen.org)

dayToDay.notes: EXPLO is explicitly an 'unplugged' program - device use is restricted as a stated program value, not merely a default policy. Residential students live in Wellesley College dorms with roommates, supported by Resident Advisors around the clock; a general staff-to-student ratio of 1:7 is advertised. Weekends are student-choice: options include whale watching, Red Sox games, museum visits, and other off-campus trips, with a 24/7 health center on site. Day students follow the same academic day as residential students but go home at night; if a day student stays for evening programming, a $38 dinner + evening event fee is charged to their account. International students live alongside domestic students in the same dorms and dining halls.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: EXPLO program details and tuition/FAQ pages (explo.org)

dayToDay.notes: Discover-tier programs (2 weeks) are staff-led group experiences with daily supervision, no host-family placement, and no Spanish requirement - the lowest-independence entry point. Explore-tier (3-3.5 weeks) and Immerse-tier (4 weeks) programs place students individually with a host family, with growing independence and responsibility as program length increases; Spanish proficiency requirements grow accordingly. A 24/7 on-call safety and mental-wellness support system is reachable regardless of location. Flights, travel insurance, and gear are not included in the program fee and must be arranged separately.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: AMIGOS Programs and Costs & Access pages (amigosinternational.org)

dayToDay.notes: Same organization-wide tier structure as other AMIGOS countries: Explore and Immerse programs here place students with host families; independence and Spanish expectations increase with program length. 24/7 safety support applies regardless of country. Flights and travel insurance are not included in the fee.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: AMIGOS Programs and Costs & Access pages (amigosinternational.org)

dayToDay.notes: Discover-tier programs here are staff-led group experiences with no host family placement and no Spanish requirement. Explore-tier places students individually with a host family, with independence and Spanish expectations growing accordingly. A 24/7 on-call safety and mental-wellness support system applies. Flights and travel insurance are not included in the program fee.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: AMIGOS Programs page (amigosinternational.org)

dayToDay.notes: Paraguay only offers Explore and Immerse tiers (no Discover, no Middle School) - the most independence-focused country in the org's lineup. Tierra Guarani (6 weeks) is the single longest program AMIGOS offers anywhere, including Spanish AND Guarani-language practice alongside homestay life.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: AMIGOS Programs page (amigosinternational.org)

dayToDay.notes: Students travel as a single group of 12 with 3 adult leaders throughout the trip, camping in the backcountry (San Juan National Forest) for the backpacking segment and along the riverbank during the 2-day whitewater rafting section, with no fixed base camp. Group meets and disbands in Denver, CO. As with all Moondance trips, the program is explicitly 'unplugged' - phones and social media use are restricted as a stated program value - and there is no routine parent contact during the trip itself.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Moondance Adventures Colorado Trail trip page and general FAQ pages (moondanceadventures.com)

dayToDay.notes: Students travel as a single small group (typically around 12 students with 3 adult leaders) for the entire trip, camping or staying in group accommodations rather than with host families, with no fixed home base for most of the itinerary. The program is explicitly 'unplugged' - phone and social media use is restricted as a stated program value, not just a default policy - and there is no routine parent contact during the trip. Groups meet at a designated point at the start of the trip and disband at the same or a nearby point at the end.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Moondance Adventures general FAQ and About/Why Moondance pages (moondanceadventures.com)

dayToDay.notes: Students travel in small, mixed-gender groups led by trip leaders, camping or staying in group accommodations for the trip's duration rather than a fixed home base for most itineraries. Trips are rated on a 10-point Challenge Level scale specific to each program, so families can gauge physical difficulty before enrolling. Groups meet at a designated point (often an airport) to start the trip and disband at a similar point at the end.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Apogee Adventures trip pages and FAQ (apogeeadventures.com)

dayToDay.notes: Days center on collaborative writing sessions with a professional writing instructor, working individually and in small groups to develop each student's college essay. Time is split between structured writing workshops and exploring Maine's coastline.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Apogee Adventures College Prep program page (apogeeadventures.com)

dayToDay.notes: Includes a rural homestay experience (bamboo weaving, tie-dye, tea cultivation with a local host family) plus a night in floating huts on Khao Sok National Park's lake. All trip leaders are Wilderness First Responder and CPR certified.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Bold Earth Thailand trip page

dayToDay.notes: Students travel hut-to-hut through the Alps, staying in mountain huts (some with showers) rather than camping or hotels, alongside some hostel-chalet nights. All trip leaders are Wilderness First Responder and CPR certified.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Bold Earth site homepage and blog references to Alps/Dolomites hut-to-hut travel

dayToDay.notes: Students travel hut-to-hut through the Dolomites, staying in mountain huts rather than camping or hotels for most of the trip - explicitly named by Bold Earth as one of the few international trips that also includes tent camping on certain nights. All trip leaders are Wilderness First Responder and CPR certified.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Bold Earth site homepage and blog ('7 Outdoor Skills')

dayToDay.notes: A domestic trip with confirmed tent camping as part of the itinerary (explicitly named among Bold Earth's camping-inclusive trips), alongside urban exploration in San Francisco. All trip leaders are Wilderness First Responder and CPR certified.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Bold Earth blog ('7 Outdoor Skills') and California trip page

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation type varies by specific trip; most trips use a mix of camping, hostels, guesthouses, and (on a few trips) hotels, with the exact nightly breakdown detailed in each trip's own itinerary. Only a minority of trips are full-camping the entire time. All trip leaders are Wilderness First Responder and CPR certified. Students are met at the airport by trip leaders and call home as soon as they've joined the group; regular family updates continue via blog posts and photos, though students are not in direct phone contact during the trip.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Bold Earth FAQ and blog ('Is Bold Earth Right for Me?') pages (boldearth.com)

dayToDay.notes: Wilderness Adventures is explicitly a screen-free program - unplugging is presented as a core program value, not just a default policy. Students travel in small groups on the specific itinerary of their chosen trip, with accommodation and daily structure varying by program (detailed on each trip's own page). The organization was founded in 1973 and was formerly known as Wilderness Ventures before rebranding.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Wilderness Adventures homepage and general program pages (wildernessadventures.com)

dayToDay.notes: Students live aboard a sailing vessel for the entire program, sharing cabins with a small crew of peers and instructors. Days are structured around the boat's itinerary - sailing between islands, scuba instruction and dives, and shore stops for excursions - with instructors present around the clock in the shared living space. There is no fixed land base; the boat itself is the accommodation throughout.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Broadreach High School program pages, each explicitly labeled a 'liveaboard adventure' (gobroadreach.com)

dayToDay.notes: Students are based out of a fixed facility for the program's duration - a research station, dive lodge, or similar - rather than living aboard a boat. Days are built around the program's core activity (fieldwork, clinical/animal-care work, or shore-based diving), with day trips or excursions from that home base as part of the itinerary.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Broadreach High School program pages, each explicitly labeled a 'land-based adventure' (gobroadreach.com)

dayToDay.notes: Students live aboard a sailing vessel or catamaran for the entire program, sharing space with a small crew of peers and instructors experienced in working with this younger age group. Days are structured around the boat's itinerary - sailing between islands, scuba/snorkel instruction, and shore stops - with instructors present around the clock. There is no fixed land base; the boat itself is the accommodation throughout.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Broadreach Middle School program pages, each explicitly labeled a 'liveaboard adventure' (gobroadreach.com)

dayToDay.notes: Students are based out of a fixed facility for the program's duration rather than living aboard a boat, with instructors experienced in working with this younger age group. Days are built around the program's core activity (diving instruction or wildlife engagement), with excursions from that home base as part of the itinerary.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Broadreach Middle School program pages, each explicitly labeled a 'land-based adventure/program' (gobroadreach.com)

dayToDay.notes: Commuter day program on the WPI campus: instruction runs 9am-4pm Monday-Friday. Students choose one or more weekly sessions and a STEM course track for each week; weeks are offered on a rolling basis across the summer (four distinct weeks in 2027). Lunch is not included in tuition for commuter programs.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: WPI Ignite program page (wpi.edu)

dayToDay.notes: Commuter day program on the WPI campus: instruction runs 9am-4pm Monday-Friday for one week. Students choose a single STEM course track (robotics, aerospace, forensics, video game design, etc.) taught by WPI faculty through hands-on labs, demos, and discussions.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: WPI Launch program page (wpi.edu)

dayToDay.notes: Five-week session taking a real WPI undergraduate course for transferable college credit at 50% off standard summer tuition. Students may enroll in person on the Worcester campus, live online (synchronous), or on demand (asynchronous); WPI recommends one course per session. On-campus housing is not available — in-person students commute or arrange their own housing. Course materials average about $200 per course and are purchased separately.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: WPI High-Achieving High School Students program page (wpi.edu)

dayToDay.notes: Students live on the WPI campus for the session, exploring a STEM major paired with a humanities or business minor, alongside peers from around the world. The program emphasizes building independence and leadership skills within a structured but immersive 'preview of college life' format, including field trips and organized workshops.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: WPI Frontiers overview page (wpi.edu)

dayToDay.notes: Students live in an MIT dorm alongside the MIT undergraduate students who serve as teaching assistants. Daily required classes run Monday-Friday from approximately 9:30am-5pm, with occasional evening hours, plus some planned weekend academic field trips and social outings. The schedule includes classes, labs, homework, and unstructured social time with other WTP students. Students are expected to have no other significant time commitments during the four weeks. A laptop is expected for coursework; free loaners are available for students who need one.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: MIT WTP calendar and FAQ pages (wtp.mit.edu)

dayToDay.notes: This is a highly structured, academically intensive residential program: the daily schedule runs from 7am breakfast to 10pm, with classes and research in the morning, problem sessions or additional classes in the afternoon, and study groups in the evening. Campers are explicitly not permitted to take online courses or participate in any other program, in person or online, during the six weeks. Parent visits during camp are allowed but require prior approval through a request form, rather than being either fully open or fully prohibited.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Mathworks HSMC program page and Camps visit-request page (txst.edu/mathworks)

dayToDay.notes: Students live in a campus dormitory supervised by camp counselors at a ratio of 1 counselor to 4 students - closer supervision than the HSMC high schooler program. Days include daily math classes taught by university professors, study group sessions, and recreation time with free use of the university's Student Recreation Center (basketball, volleyball, racquetball, indoor track, pool). Fridays include a guest lecture from an academic or industry speaker followed by a picnic with games at a local park. As with HSMC, campers are not permitted to take online courses or participate in any other program during the two weeks.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Mathworks JSMCR program page and JSMCR Daily Schedule and Events page (txst.edu/mathworks)

dayToDay.notes: Residential students live in a dorm-style facility in Manhattan, with roommates assigned by gender identity and age. Building security and residential staff are present in the residence hall 24/7, and Residential Directors live adjacent to the students they oversee. Both residential and day students participate in a structured set of evening and weekend activities beyond the academic day. Day students commute in for the academic portion and have the option to stay for dinner and evening/weekend programming, but go home (or to their own housing) at night rather than living on-site.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: NYT Edu 'Program Experience' and NYC Summer Academy pages

dayToDay.notes: This is a day program with no overnight component - parents drop off and pick up daily, and San Marcos CISD provides bus transportation, but only for students enrolled in that local school district (families outside the district must arrange their own transportation, as Mathworks itself doesn't provide any). Breakfast, lunch, and a snack are provided during the school day. Students are on campus only during camp hours and go home each evening.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Mathworks JSMCH program page (txst.edu/mathworks)

dayToDay.notes: Students live in Penn dormitories with a meal plan in the undergraduate dining halls, described by the program as including 'student supervision.' The schedule is described as extremely rigorous and non-stop given that a full college credit is earned in just three weeks. Meals are provided twice daily Monday-Friday and twice on Sunday, but there are no provided meals at all on Saturdays, which are reserved for excursions and off-campus activities - students should budget for that. Full attendance is mandatory from the first day to the last; the program does not permit partial attendance or early departure under any circumstances, since credit is tied to completing the full three weeks.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: M&TSI program page and FAQs (fisher.wharton.upenn.edu)

dayToDay.notes: Students live in double suite-style dorm rooms with bathrooms on the hall, with faculty and residential staff (Deans, Student Deans, Junior Deans, and Health & Activity Coordinators) living in the same residence halls, focused specifically on student life and well-being. The academic day is structured: major seminar meets six days a week for three hours, minor seminar meets three days a week for two hours, with afternoons/evenings open for electives and extracurriculars, and evening programming (guest speakers, shows, or college-admissions Q&As) bringing all seminar groups together after dinner. Breakfasts and dinners are provided at the dorm cafeteria, but lunches are not included in tuition - students handle lunch independently in small peer groups, a mix of city restaurants and picnics. On weekends, students go on staff-led or seminar-group excursions, which may include a day trip to New York City.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Oxford Academia at Yale program page (oxfordacademia.com)

dayToDay.notes: Day students attend roughly 9:45am-4pm; residential students live in NYU-area dormitory housing with lounges, computer rooms, and laundry facilities, with staff living in residence. Uniquely among SOCAPA's campuses, meals are NOT included in the Manhattan residential fee - students are responsible for purchasing their own food. For the first three days, counselors guide students to nearby restaurants and delis in Greenwich Village/East Village; after that, students sign out and explore food options in self-organized small groups (never alone, per policy). Every weekday evening (Monday-Friday) a planned activity is scheduled - a campus barbecue, a dinner out in the city, a pool visit, a theater or musical performance, or a film screening. Saturday afternoons not spent shooting/rehearsing are reserved for a group excursion (past examples include Coney Island, Broadway shows, and various museums), and at least once per session SOCAPA brings in an industry professional (actors, writers, directors) to lead a master class open to all students regardless of track. Unlike other SOCAPA campuses, there is no unaccompanied-minor airport pickup/drop-off service offered at all at the NYC campus.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: SOCAPA NYC campus page and SOCAPA Tuition & Costs page (socapa.org)

dayToDay.notes: Residential students live in Occidental College dorms with double/triple occupancy, and meals are included: three meals a day, Monday-Friday, at the campus cafeteria, plus one off-campus group dinner per session.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: SOCAPA LA campus page and SOCAPA Tuition & Costs page (socapa.org)

dayToDay.notes: Residential students live in Champlain College dorms with double/triple occupancy. Meals are included: three meals a day, Monday-Friday, at the campus cafeteria, plus one off-campus group dinner per session. VT uniquely offers optional 35mm/darkroom photography work (Core and Advanced Photography).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: SOCAPA Tuition & Costs page and individual track pages (socapa.org)

dayToDay.notes: Residential students live in suite-style housing at Delta Terrace in Sunset Village, with their own bathroom, and staff (residence life coordinators among them) living in the same halls. A typical day: 8am wake-up, 8:30 breakfast, 9:30-11:30 morning course, 11:30 lunch (unstructured - students choose where to eat in small groups, on or off campus), 1:30-3:30 afternoon course, then free time until 6pm dinner, followed by organized evening activities. Breakfast and dinner are included in tuition; lunch is explicitly NOT included and is handled independently by students. Commuter (day) students attend roughly 9:30am-3:30/4pm on class days only, are not housed overnight, have no meals included, get limited access to UCLA recreational facilities, and may optionally join group field trips or the college-admissions workshops.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA 14-day and 21-day program pages (westcoastconnection.com)

dayToDay.notes: The first three weeks follow the standard UCLA pre-college schedule: suite-style housing at Delta Terrace, morning and afternoon courses, breakfast and dinner included (lunch paid separately), evening activities, and LA excursions. The program then continues with a 6-day Hawaii extension to Maui and Oahu, including snorkeling, a traditional luau, and travel by private coach between islands. Internal flights from Los Angeles to Hawaii and between islands cost an additional $850 beyond tuition; airfare to Los Angeles at the start and home from Oahu at the end are also not included. There is no commuter option for this itinerary.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection UCLA plus Hawaii Extension program page (westcoastconnection.com)

dayToDay.notes: Students live in two-person suites at the Kadora Sarria Barcelona Residence, each with a private bathroom, air conditioning, and Wi-Fi; the residence has 24-hour security. A typical day: 8am wake-up, 8:30 breakfast, 10:30 morning course, 1pm lunch (unstructured - students choose where to eat in small groups), 3pm group afternoon excursion/highlight, 5:30pm 'Student's Choice' free time (sports, pool, fitness club, or city exploring), 8pm dinner (some nights at the residence, some nights out as a group or in smaller groups at local restaurants), and evening activities until 10pm. Breakfast and dinner are included in tuition; lunch is not.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection Barcelona 21-day program page (westcoastconnection.com)

dayToDay.notes: The first three weeks follow the standard Barcelona pre-college schedule at the Kadora Sarria residence: morning course, unstructured lunch, afternoon highlights, and included breakfast and dinner. The program then continues with a grand finale week touring the Amalfi Coast (Sorrento, Capri, Positano) and Rome before returning home from Rome. An additional $245 internal flight from Spain to Italy is required beyond tuition; airfare to Barcelona at the start and home from Rome at the end are also not included.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection Barcelona plus Amalfi Coast & Rome program page (westcoastconnection.com)

dayToDay.notes: The first three weeks follow the standard Barcelona pre-college schedule at the Kadora Sarria residence: morning course, unstructured lunch, afternoon highlights, and included breakfast and dinner. The program then continues with a 9-day grand finale in Greece (Athens, Naxos, and Santorini), including scuba and snorkeling opportunities. An additional $495 internal flight from Spain to Greece is required beyond tuition; airfare to Barcelona at the start and home from Athens at the end are also not included.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection Barcelona plus Greek Islands program page (westcoastconnection.com)

dayToDay.notes: Students live in single-occupancy rooms at The Social Hub Belfiore Florence Residence, each with air conditioning, Wi-Fi, a private bathroom, and a personal workstation; the residence has 24-hour security, laundry, a gym, and a rooftop pool. A typical day: 8:30am wake-up, 9am breakfast, 10:30am morning course, 1pm lunch (unstructured - students choose where to eat in small groups at local cafés and restaurants), 3pm group afternoon highlight, 5:30pm 'Student's Choice' free time (sports, gym, staff-planned activity, or city exploration), 8:30pm dinner (some nights at the residence, some nights out as a group or in smaller groups at local restaurants), and evening activities until roughly 10:15pm. Breakfast and dinner are included in tuition; lunch is not.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection Florence 14-day and 21-day program pages (westcoastconnection.com)

dayToDay.notes: The first three weeks follow the standard Florence pre-college schedule at The Social Hub Belfiore (including a Venice weekend getaway), then the program continues with a grand finale week touring the Amalfi Coast (Sorrento, Capri, Positano) and Rome before returning home from Rome. Airfare to Florence at the start and home from Rome at the end are not included in tuition.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection Florence plus Amalfi Coast & Rome program page (westcoastconnection.com)

dayToDay.notes: The first three weeks follow the standard Florence pre-college schedule at The Social Hub Belfiore (including a Venice weekend getaway), then the program continues with a 9-day grand finale in the Greek Islands (Athens, Naxos, and Santorini), including scuba and snorkeling opportunities. An additional $345 internal flight from Italy to Greece is required beyond tuition; airfare to Florence at the start and home from Athens at the end are also not included.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection Florence plus Greek Islands program page (westcoastconnection.com)

dayToDay.notes: Residential students live at Residence La Citadelle, McGill University, in individual twin-bed rooms with private bathrooms, air conditioning, housekeeping service, and a personal work desk. A typical day: 8am wake-up, 8:30 breakfast, 10am morning course (or start of a full-day track option), lunch break (unstructured - students choose where to eat in small groups), 2pm afternoon course, then free time ('Student's Choice') until 7pm dinner, followed by evening activities until around 9pm. Breakfast and dinner are included in tuition; lunch is not and is handled independently by students. Commuter (day) students attend roughly 10am-4/4:30pm on class days only, are not housed overnight, have no meals included, get limited access to McGill's recreational facilities, and may optionally join the college-admissions workshops.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Westcoast Connection Montreal 14-day and 21-day program pages (westcoastconnection.com)

dayToDay.notes: Students stay primarily on a private Caribbean island for the SCUBA portion of the trip, with some time on the mainland for cultural excursions. Transportation includes shuttles, vans, and a private boat to the island. Showers are available most days; there is no machine laundry, so handwashing/air-drying is expected. All trip leaders are certified Wilderness First Responders.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ARCC Belize program page (arccprograms.com)

dayToDay.notes: Students camp in tents (3-4 per tent, supplied by ARCC) at front-country campgrounds and state parks - meaning always close to the group's van, with restroom facilities and running water, and showers at many sites. The group travels together in a 15-passenger van with their two leaders, and works together to plan and cook meals throughout the trip.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ARCC California program page

dayToDay.notes: An entirely camping-based program; students sleep in tents at front-country campgrounds across National Parks, State Parks, and National Forest land, with restroom facilities, running water, and some on-site showers. The group travels together in a 15-passenger van with a small trailer, which serves as their home base, and prepares meals together as a group.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ARCC Yellowstone & Grand Teton program page

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation varies across the trip: hotels, rustic camping shelters, a jungle lodge, and dorm-style bungalows. Transportation is by private bus/van arranged by ARCC's in-country partner. All trip leaders are certified Wilderness First Responders.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ARCC Bali & Sumatra program page

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation varies: Moroccan riads, local Spanish homes, hotels, and an Amazigh community guesthouse in the High Atlas Mountains. Travel includes private shuttles, vans, trains, and a ferry crossing of the Strait of Gibraltar. All trip leaders are certified Wilderness First Responders.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ARCC Spain & Morocco program page

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation varies: simple hotels, hostels, homestays, and a village community house. Travel is by train and private bus. All trip leaders are certified Wilderness First Responders. High altitude (Cusco is over 11,000 feet) - the itinerary builds in acclimatization time.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ARCC Peru program page

dayToDay.notes: Students live with homestay families in a highland ranching village for the service portion, and stay at a river lodge during the rafting segment of the trip.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ARCC Costa Rica program page and third-party comparison sources

dayToDay.notes: Includes village homestays and an off-grid eco-retreat in Fiji's highlands, plus beach camping in Fiji and more conventional accommodation in Australia (Sydney, Queensland).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ARCC Australia & Fiji program page and TeenLife listing

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation varies: hostels, small simple hotels, an eco-lodge, and rustic community buildings. Travel is by private bus, boat, and a commercial flight to/from the Galapagos. All trip leaders are certified Wilderness First Responders.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ARCC Ecuador & Galapagos program page

dayToDay.notes: Mostly camping in private campsites (tents and gear provided by ARCC), with some nights in a small hotel on Zanzibar and a guesthouse in Southern Kenya. Travel is via custom-built overland safari trucks equipped with sleeping/kitchen/storage facilities. All trip leaders are certified Wilderness First Responders.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ARCC Kenya & Tanzania program page

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation varies: small hotels and hostels, guesthouses, and a sailboat overnight in Halong Bay. Travel includes private buses, boats, commercial flights, and tuk-tuks. All trip leaders are certified Wilderness First Responders.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: ARCC Vietnam & Cambodia program page

dayToDay.notes: Residential Middle School students have dedicated floors exclusively for Summer Discovery in Centennial Hall, fully air-conditioned, near basketball/tennis courts and open fields. Commuter students specifically at the Middle School level are NOT permitted to attend evening or off-campus activities/excursions - a real restriction distinct from the High School commuter policy, which does allow broader participation.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Summer Discovery UCLA campus page and third-party summer program aggregator (summerapply.com), cross-referenced against confirmed current pricing

dayToDay.notes: At UCLA, High School students have an exclusive residence hall not shared with any other program (Hedrick Summit), fully air-conditioned. Tuition includes academic instruction, housing, 2 meals/day (lunch and dinner), and extracurricular activities/excursions every afternoon, evening, and weekend, plus use of athletic/recreation facilities. International students pay an additional registration fee ($379 residential / $239 commuter) covering medical insurance and airport transfers. A completion certificate and letter of recognition are issued per course/academy taken.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Summer Discovery UCLA campus page (summerdiscovery.com)

dayToDay.notes: Runs alongside Yale's High School Institute for the Gifted program on the same campus during the same 3-week window (Jul 3-23), though with separate staff, classes, and age-appropriate structure per Summer Discovery's general policy of keeping Middle School and High School operationally distinct. Tuition includes 2-3 meals per day, 7 days per week, plus extracurricular activities and excursions every afternoon, evening, and weekend, and use of athletic/recreation facilities.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Summer Discovery Yale University campus page (High School-level confirmation); Middle-School-specific policy details not independently confirmed for this campus.

dayToDay.notes: Tuition includes 2-3 meals per day, 7 days per week, plus extracurricular activities and excursions every afternoon, evening, and weekend, and use of athletic/recreation facilities. International students pay an additional registration fee ($379 residential / $239 commuter) covering medical insurance and airport transfers; international students fly into JFK, domestic students into Bradley Intl (BDL).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Summer Discovery Yale University campus page (summerdiscovery.com)

dayToDay.notes: Students have unparalleled access to Berkeley's labs, maker spaces, and research facilities as part of coursework. International students pay an additional $379 registration fee (residential only mentioned) covering medical insurance and airport transfers; the recommended airport is SFO.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Summer Discovery UC Berkeley campus page (summerdiscovery.com)

dayToDay.notes: This campus's 2-week track is Academy-only (no Individual Course/AM+PM option at that length); the 3-week track offers both Individual Courses and Academies.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Summer Discovery UT Austin campus and course listing pages (summerdiscovery.com)

dayToDay.notes: Structured as one-week course modules with a two-week minimum enrollment; nearly the entire course roster (Individual Courses and Academies alike) repeats identically across all three 2-week sessions, so a family's choice of session mainly comes down to timing rather than course availability. Students can combine two consecutive 2-week sessions into a 4-week stay at a discount versus booking them separately.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Summer Discovery University of Michigan campus and course listing pages (summerdiscovery.com)

dayToDay.notes: Bryn Mawr's campus is noted for its architecture, often compared to Hogwarts. This is a commuter-only campus (no residential option). Included in the day: supervised outdoor playtime with games/sports (weather permitting), lunch daily at the Dining Commons, and mid-class outdoor breaks in the courtyard. The best airport for families flying in is Philadelphia International (PHL).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Summer Discovery Bryn Mawr College campus page (summerdiscovery.com)

dayToDay.notes: Runs with separate staff, schedule, and activities from Georgetown's High School program, consistent with Summer Discovery's general policy of keeping Middle School and High School operationally distinct even on the same campus.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Summer Discovery general Middle School program pages (summerdiscovery.com)

dayToDay.notes: Located in Washington, D.C., giving students proximity to policy, law, and government institutions relevant to several of the campus's course topics (International Relations, Governing America, Careers in Law). Individual Courses programs include one morning and one afternoon pick.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Summer Discovery Georgetown University campus and course listing pages (summerdiscovery.com)

dayToDay.notes: All-Academy campus (no Individual Courses) with six distinct, overlapping 2-week windows rolling through the summer, rather than 2–3 sequential blocks like other Summer Discovery campuses. Grades 9–11 only — excludes rising/current seniors, narrower than the 9–12 band used at every other Summer Discovery campus.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Summer Discovery Dartmouth campus and course listing pages (summerdiscovery.com)

dayToDay.notes: A shorter, middle-school-appropriate version of GLA's community service model, run with separate staffing/structure from the ages-14-18 Adventures track (consistent with how other orgs in this catalog separate their middle school and high school programs).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: GLA Costa Rica Middle School Service Adventure program page (experiencegla.com)

dayToDay.notes: GLA programs combine hands-on service or research work (conservation, healthcare, education, community development, depending on the specific program's theme) with cultural excursions and adventure activities, all in a residential group format. Programs are organized by Global Leadership Adventures, a Terra Education-family brand (sibling to Summer Springboard).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: GLA program guide and general program pages (experiencegla.com)

dayToDay.notes: Overland is explicitly screen-free as a stated program value, and is accredited by the American Camp Association. Groups are small (typically capped at 10-12 students) and are usually a mix of two adjacent grades. Meals are prepared as group projects rather than served to students. Students fly into a specific gateway city/airport per trip, where Overland leaders provide supervised arrival and departure - the exact city varies by trip (e.g., Anchorage for Alaska trips, Zurich for Alpine Challenge, Bozeman for Montana trips). Camping style varies by trip - primarily frontcountry (with facilities) for some, extended backcountry/backpacking for others - detailed on each trip's own page. Overland has run since 1984.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Overland Summers trip pages, FAQ, and general marketing pages (overlandsummers.com)

dayToDay.notes: Itinerary includes an ATV-style itinerary with canyoning through jungle waterfalls, a visit to the Rio Negro hot springs (six pools naturally heated by the Rincon de la Vieja Volcano), a volcanic mud bath, and time at Tamarindo Beach. Paced more relaxed than the 9-10 grade equivalent trip to ease first-time travelers into being abroad.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Costa Rica for Middle School: Adrenaline program page

dayToDay.notes: First night at a mountain lodge overlooking a volcano in Turrialba, followed by an overnight whitewater rafting trip on the Pacuare River with a night spent in a rainforest lodge along the riverbank. Community service work (~20 hours) takes place alongside adventure activities. Designed specifically to be a gentle first international trip for younger travelers.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Costa Rica for Middle School: Hola Costa Rica program page

dayToDay.notes: Combines elements from the org's other Costa Rica programs into one extended trip: canyoning, hot springs, a volcanic mud bath, beachside community service (cleanups, English teaching), ziplining, and whitewater rafting. As with all TFT programs, specific accommodation names are not published in advance for safety reasons.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Costa Rica for Middle School: Ultimate Adventure & Service program page

dayToDay.notes: TFT does not publish specific accommodation names for safety reasons (families get this after registering, via a secure parent portal) - generally small, centrally located, family-run hotels rather than large chain hotels. Tuition includes ground transportation, accommodation, chaperones/guides, program activities, taxes/tips, and all meals; airfare, visas, and personal expenses are not included, though an optional group flight is typically offered. Over 75% of TFT travelers come independently (not with a friend), which the org frames as encouraging new friendships. Dietary restrictions (vegetarian, vegan, gluten-free, etc.) are fully accommodated.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Costa Rica Service program page and general Costa Rica destination page (travelforteens.com)

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation includes hotels, lodges, and a more rustic jungle lodge. Community service takes place at a sustainable farm on the Galápagos Islands (recycling, cooking in a traditional mud oven). As with all TFT programs, specific accommodation names are not published in advance for safety reasons - families get this via a secure parent portal after registering.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Ecuador & the Galápagos Service program page

dayToDay.notes: Students stay on a private island accessible via a short flight into Placencia followed by a boat crossing. Daily structure centers on the marine conservation organization's own programming - PADI certification progress for beginners, or direct volunteer diving work for already-certified students - plus expert-led talks on topics like invasive lionfish control and ocean plastic pollution.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Belize Scuba & Service program page

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation is a mix of 3-star hotels and a homestay in the village of Misminay, where students sleep in a private room attached to a local family's home, with shared restrooms and communal meals in the village center. One evening involves helping the host community prepare a traditional pachamanca meal cooked in the earth.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Peru Service program page

dayToDay.notes: Combines the day-to-day structure of both standalone programs in sequence: the Peru Service homestay/community-service segment first, followed directly by the Ecuador & the Galápagos Service segment (farm, hotels, and lodge accommodation) - see each standalone program's notes for details on its respective portion.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Peru, Ecuador & the Galápagos Service program page

dayToDay.notes: Highlights across the Oceania programs include diving/snorkeling the Great Barrier Reef, sailing through the Whitsunday Islands, hiking/spotting wildlife in the Australian Outback, and (on the Fiji leg specifically) a traditional kava ceremony and community engagement in a coastal village. As with all TFT programs, specific accommodation names are not published in advance for safety reasons.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Oceania destination page and general program marketing

dayToDay.notes: General TFT Africa policy: accommodation names are not published in advance for safety reasons - families access this via a secure parent portal after registering. Vaccinations are the family's responsibility to arrange via their own doctor; TFT provides general guidance but does not mandate specific vaccines.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Africa destination page (general policy, not Tanzania-specific)

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation varies significantly by stop: a modern hotel in Johannesburg's Sandton area, en-suite dormitory rooms (max 4 students/room) in Kruger and Plettenberg Bay, clifftop lodging overlooking the Wild Coast in Chintsa, beach-bungalow-style cabins near Addo National Park, and a modern boutique hotel in Cape Town. Packing note: students must bring their own work gloves and clothes/closed-toe shoes that can get paint on them for the service portion; TFT supplies all tools/materials on-site. US citizens receive a free 90-day tourist visa on arrival.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Ultimate South Africa Service & Safari program page

dayToDay.notes: As with all TFT programs, specific accommodation names are not published in advance for safety reasons - families access this via a secure parent portal after registering. Program lengths across Asia range from 10 to 26 days, with single-country trips typically 10-17 days and multi-country combination trips extending up to nearly four weeks.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Asia destination page (travelforteens.com/asia)

dayToDay.notes: As with TFT's other Middle School itineraries, pacing is more relaxed than the equivalent grades 9-10 versions, designed to ease younger, often first-time-abroad travelers into group travel. As with all TFT programs, specific accommodation names are not published in advance for safety reasons.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens United States destination page and general Middle School program framing (travelforteens.com/unitedstates)

dayToDay.notes: TFT's Middle School Europe itineraries are consistently described as relaxed-pace versions of the equivalent high school trips - fewer overnight-city transitions, slower daily rhythm, and designed to ease first-time-abroad travelers into group travel. As with all TFT programs, specific accommodation names are not published in advance for safety reasons.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Europe country destination pages (France, Italy, Greece, Spain, Portugal)

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation is a mix of modern hotels and comfortable, unique family-run lodging, all vetted and supervised by trip leaders present 24/7. As with all TFT programs, specific accommodation names are not published in advance for safety reasons. Alaska activities include sea kayaking, hiking near glaciers, whitewater rafting, and a sled-cart ride with husky puppies.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens United States destination page (travelforteens.com/unitedstates)

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation is a mix of modern hotels and comfortable, unique family-run lodging, all vetted and supervised by trip leaders present 24/7. As with all TFT programs, specific accommodation names are not published in advance for safety reasons. Alaska activities include sea kayaking, hiking near glaciers, whitewater rafting, and a sled-cart ride with husky puppies; Hawaii activities include surfing, snorkeling (including night snorkeling with manta rays), and sea turtle conservation work (reef surveying, beach cleanup).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens United States destination page (travelforteens.com/unitedstates)

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation is a mix of modern hotels and comfortable, unique family-run lodging, all vetted and supervised by trip leaders present 24/7. As with all TFT programs, specific accommodation names are not published in advance for safety reasons. Hawaii activities include surfing, snorkeling (including night snorkeling with manta rays), and sea turtle conservation work (reef surveying, beach cleanup).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens United States destination page (travelforteens.com/unitedstates)

dayToDay.notes: Service and adventure program specifically on the Big Island and Kauai, distinct from the multi-island 'Island Hopping' program.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens United States destination page

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation includes hotels and, on some nights, alpine lodging near the base of a mountain. High-ropes and canyoning activities are a structured part of the itinerary, not optional add-ons.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Switzerland destination page

dayToDay.notes: Includes formal French classes taught by native speakers as a structured part of the day, alongside cultural excursions.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens France destination page

dayToDay.notes: Community service work varies by program (island-based service projects, sea turtle conservation). Accommodation is centrally located, often steps from the sea on the islands. Meals emphasize authentic tavernas over tourist-oriented restaurants.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Greece destination page

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation is centrally located, often steps from the sea on the islands. Meals emphasize authentic tavernas over tourist-oriented restaurants.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Greece destination page

dayToDay.notes: Island-hopping structure means frequent movement between destinations (e.g., Santorini, Paros, Corfu) rather than a single home base for the trip.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Greece destination page

dayToDay.notes: As with all TFT programs, specific accommodation names are not published in advance for safety reasons. Italian meal timing runs later than in the US (lunch 1-2:30pm, dinner rarely before 7:30-8:30pm), with an early-evening Aperitivo custom before dinner.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Italy destination page

dayToDay.notes: Includes formal Spanish classes as a structured part of the day. Spanish meal timing runs later than in the US (lunch 2-4pm, dinner 8-9pm), with tapas culture as a core part of the food experience.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Spain destination page

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation is safe, comfortable, centrally-located hotels, all rooms supervised by staff.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Portugal destination page

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation is primarily family-run guesthouses and hostels rather than American-style hotels, reflecting Iceland's rural character; guests are typically asked to remove shoes indoors. Structured as a road trip - the group changes location most days rather than having a fixed home base.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Iceland Adventure program page

dayToDay.notes: Accommodation includes hostels for two of the three stops and an outdoor activity center on Achill Island for the third, where daily programming (surfing, canoeing, coasteering, archery) runs continuously rather than being a single scheduled activity. Traditional Irish music sessions take place in family-friendly pubs, where teens can enjoy food and soft drinks alongside the music. As with all TFT programs, specific accommodation names are not published in advance for safety reasons.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Travel For Teens Ireland destination page and customer testimonials (travelforteens.com/ireland)

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based; host families share daily meals. Daily language classes (15-20 hrs/week) paired with afternoon cultural activities in the Latin Quarter and Montmartre. Weekend excursions to Versailles and the medieval village of Provins. Morning classes and afternoon activities may swap depending on the day.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE French Language & Culture (Paris) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing (not homestay). Daily design workshops building toward a student-pitched architectural design and a 3-D model; urban sketching sessions built into the itinerary. Visits to Fondation Louis Vuitton and Musée du Quai Branly. Weekend excursions to Versailles and Provins.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Architecture & French Culture (Paris) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing. Hands-on cooking workshops twice weekly at Le Cordon Bleu's Paris campus, plus visits to fresh food markets and a cheese monger. Program culminates in a two-part team cooking competition (a main dish and dessert) judged by a panel, alongside a capstone menu presentation.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Culinary Arts & French Culture (Paris) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing. Students source recycled materials from Montmartre thrift shops and the Marché St. Pierre fabric market, working with a professional seamstress. Program culminates in a student-run Global Navigator fashion show at Galeries Lafayette.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Fashion Design & French Culture (Paris) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing. Includes an Airbus Blagnac factory tour and a from-scratch student rocket-building workshop (teams of 2-3), culminating in a live rocket launch. Excursion to Pic du Midi observatory.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Engineering & Aerospace (Toulouse) program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based; host families share daily meals. Daily language classes paired with afternoon cultural activities. Weekend excursions to Carcassonne and the French Mediterranean coast.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE French Language & Culture (Toulouse) program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based; host families share daily meals. Daily language classes paired with afternoon cultural activities. Weekend excursions to Mont Saint-Michel and the Brittany coastline.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE French Language & Culture (Rennes) program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based. Strict French-only 'Language Pledge' enforced in and out of class - students take a proficiency test before arrival and must demonstrate Intermediate-Low ACTFL/STAMP proficiency to be accepted. Weekly reflective language-learning surveys. Otherwise follows the same activity pattern as the standard Rennes program (Mont Saint-Michel, Brittany coastline). Note: this program cannot accommodate fully Kosher, Halal, or combined dietary restrictions due to local food options.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Honors French Language & Culture (Rennes) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing. Fieldwork-heavy: snorkeling, tide-pool exploration, field observations, and 12 hours of service-learning built into the schedule. Excursions to Monaco's Oceanographic Museum and boat tours of coastal towns. Involves moderate-to-high intensity physical activity; swimming ability not required but strongly encouraged.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Marine Ecology & Sustainability (Nice) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing. Students storyboard, shoot, and edit a five-minute short film in small teams over the course of the program, then present it to peers, teachers, and local film professionals. Includes a Seine boat tour and visits to the Louvre and Musée d'Orsay for creative inspiration.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Filmmaking & French Culture (Paris) program page

dayToDay.notes: Students stay in group housing with CIEE Program Leaders residing on-site for overnight supervision in each of the three cities the program visits (Paris, Milan, Madrid); site-wide staffing is roughly 1 Program Leader per 12 students. The program moves between cities during the three weeks, with travel days built into the schedule. A curfew applies each night, with the exact time communicated during on-program orientation. Free time is supervised under a buddy-system policy, and students are not permitted to leave the group housing site independently.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE High School Summer Abroad Housing/Safety/FAQ pages (org-wide policy, not program-specific)

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based; host families share daily meals, giving students a chance to practice Spanish at home. Daily language classes paired with afternoon cultural activities across Buenos Aires's 48 neighborhoods. Weekend excursions to an estancia (ranch) for parrillada (barbecue) and gaucho culture, plus a flight to Iguazú Falls.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Spanish Language & Argentinian Culture (Buenos Aires) program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based. Daily on-pitch training paired with sports psychology coursework (stress/anxiety management, performance zones, goal-setting). Visits La Boca neighborhood and its open-air museum, tours La Bombonera stadium (home of Boca Juniors), and includes a hands-on tango workshop with local students. Overnight stay at a traditional 19th-century estancia (ranch) with horseback riding and a traditional asado, plus a day trip to the Tigre Delta.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Soccer & Mental Performance (Buenos Aires) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing (not homestay). Field-research heavy: students collect and analyze data on sustainability strategies in urban coastal ecosystems. Excursions include Featherdale Wildlife Sanctuary, the Blue Mountains (Scenic Railway, Three Sisters rock formation), and a traditional Aboriginal Bushtucker Tour. A Manly Beach snorkeling trip is a program highlight, done in the cooler waters of the Australian winter (the Southern Hemisphere's June-August is winter).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Wildlife Conservation (Sydney) program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based at Mokolodi Nature Reserve on the outskirts of Gaborone, described by CIEE as a 'living lab.' Hands-on habitat-care work included (e.g., cleaning vulture ponds, tortoise enclosures) alongside sanctuary staff. Camping is part of the Okavango Delta excursion.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Wildlife Conservation (Gaborone) program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based; host families share home-cooked meals (e.g., seswaa, bogobe). Students conduct health assessments and help implement a health fair in a rural Botswana community, working alongside local community-based organizations. Includes a meeting with local high school students to discuss teen health challenges in the region, and an excursion to the Okavango Delta.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Leadership & Service in Public Health (Gaborone) program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based. Visits a working chocolate mega-factory (Cacau Show) to study franchise/supply-chain business models, and Tenondé Porã Indigenous Territory to learn about Guarani cultural preservation and sustainable income sources. Culminates in a team-pitched startup concept presented to local mentors, and a churrasco barbecue.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Global Entrepreneurship (São Paulo) program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based. Daily on-pitch training combined with sports psychology coursework (goal-setting, motivation, confidence); students maintain a Personal Performance Portfolio throughout. Includes a tour of the historic Pacaembu Arena and a 3-day overnight excursion to the island town of Ilhabela (beaches, whale-watching, Atlantic Forest hiking).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Soccer & Mental Performance (São Paulo) program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based. Hands-on cooking instruction in professional teaching kitchens, plus visits to bustling markets, neighborhood breakfast shops, and local restaurants. Overnight excursion to Yangzhou (birthplace of Huaiyang cuisine, one of China's four great culinary traditions). Also includes Tai Chi and Shaolin Kung Fu training, a pottery workshop, and a sunset Huangpu River cruise.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Culinary Arts & Chinese Culture (Shanghai) program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based. Hands-on fieldwork assessing city design and sustainability, with industry tours including an automated production facility and Apollo Park (autonomous driving/intelligent transportation center). Overnight excursion to Wuxi (Huishan Old Town, Lingshan Grand Buddha, Taihu Lake). Also includes a traditional 72-step Chinese ceramic-making workshop and a Huangpu River cruise.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Engineering & Renewable Energies (Shanghai) program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based. Students partner with a local organization on a real-world challenge, culminating in an AI-powered prototype. Includes a visit to a smart community center helping residents use digital tools, a martial arts workshop (Tai Chi and Shaolin Kung Fu, judged team competition), and table tennis at a club founded by Olympic champion Xu Xin. Overnight excursion to Wuxi.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE AI & Real-World Application (Shanghai) program page

dayToDay.notes: Students live with a host family (homestay) in Shanghai for the duration of the program, preparing and sharing Chinese meals together as part of daily language and cultural immersion. Three meals a day are provided overall with dietary needs accommodated, and all ground transportation once in-country, all cultural activities and excursions, and interactive language classes are included. Wi-Fi access is available at accommodations, but no international data plan or SIM card is included. Pre-departure advice and orientation are provided before travel, and CIEE provides 24/7 emergency on-site support plus comprehensive medical and travel protection (iNext Travel Insurance) throughout the program. An optional flight chaperone is available (flight cost itself is not included in tuition).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Chinese Language & Culture (Shanghai) program page, What's Included and Eligibility sections

dayToDay.notes: Farm-based living component: students milk cows, gather eggs, feed pigs, make compost, and care for seedlings in a native tree nursery. Week-long extension on the Pacific coastline for marine conservation study. Weekend excursions include El Tigre Waterfalls and Bajo del Tigre Nature Preserve (Children's Eternal Rainforest).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Ecology & Sustainability (Monteverde) program page

dayToDay.notes: Dorm/group housing. Guided photo walks and workshops led by professional photographers, covering composition, lighting, portrait, and low-light techniques. Ziplining over the Monteverde Cloud Forest canopy for aerial shots. Excursions to Santa Rosa National Park (wildlife/historic landscapes) and the Pacific coast (coastal and underwater photography).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Photography & Costa Rican Culture (Monteverde) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing. Field observation in the Monteverde Cloud Forest (capuchins, toucans, two-toed sloths); a night hike to observe nocturnal species. Excursion to the Pacific coast covering marine wildlife and lowland forest ecosystems (jaguars, tapirs). Includes ziplining and a Bajo del Tigre preserve hike.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Wildlife Conservation (Monteverde) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing. Coursework created in collaboration with the Malovani Kresleni art atelier. Includes a hands-on street art workshop (stenciling, layering, mural-scale work) with artists-in-residence, and the Invisible Exhibition - a sensory experience navigated in complete darkness, guided by blind or partially sighted guides. Overnight excursion to the medieval village of Český Krumlov.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Painting & Czech Culture (Prague) program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based. Visits to CopenHill (waste-to-energy plant doubling as a ski slope) and Hofor (the city's water utility). 3-day stay at Yduns Have, an eco-farm on Samsø island - picking strawberries, tending soil, caring for animals. Dialogue with students from The Green Youth Movement. Culminates in a student-developed climate advocacy strategy.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Climate Change Policy & Advocacy (Copenhagen) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing. Hands-on fieldwork collecting environmental data and analyzing sustainable behavior patterns; visit to CopenHill. Bike excursion to Nyhavn Harbor and the Little Mermaid statue. Travel to Samsø (world's first renewable energy island) and Youth Island (youth changemaker hub). Culminates in a proposed engineering tool for a green initiative.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Engineering & Sustainability (Copenhagen) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing; students fly between all three cities during the program. Visit to Station, a 3,700 sq. meter former police station turned student-driven innovation hub in Copenhagen. Visit to the Berlin Wall Memorial paired with a ropes course at Mount Mitte. Program culminates in a business pitch to a panel of professionals.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Global Entrepreneurship & Innovation in Europe program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based. Visits both a public hospital and a private clinic in Santiago to compare healthcare access. Students act as junior health promoters designing a health education fair. Bachata/salsa dance classes and a visit to the Centro León art center. Tubing and rope-swing excursion in the Mao region.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Leadership & Service in Public Health (Santiago de los Caballeros) program page

dayToDay.notes: Homestay-based. Partners with NGO Acción Callejera to run a summer camp for underprivileged children - coaching activities, running workshops, environmental clean-up projects. Visit to the Museum of Mirabal Sisters with a guided reflection on activism and social justice. Functional Spanish classes. Excursions to mountain areas and coastal cacao farms.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Leadership & Service in Youth Development (Santiago de los Caballeros) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing. Overnight excursion to Milton Keynes: Bletchley Park (WWII codebreaking site) and The National Museum of Computing (rebuilt Colossus computer). Day trip to Cambridge including the AI Animal Chat interactive exhibit and river punting. Also visits Sandbox VR (Stranger Things: Catalyst) and the Twist Museum.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE AI & Real-World Application (London) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing. Charles Dickens walking tour and a literary tour of Oxford (Alice in Wonderland/Narnia/Tolkien sites). Overnight excursion to Shakespeare's birthplace, Stratford-upon-Avon. Culminates in an Open Mic session sharing student work.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Creative Writing & British Culture (London) program page

dayToDay.notes: Group housing. Walking tour of iconic London/Greenwich filming locations (Bridgerton, Thor, Pirates of the Caribbean). Harry Potter Studio Tour. Weekend excursions to Oxford and Stratford-upon-Avon. Students produce and present a 5-minute film scene with a director's statement.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: CIEE Filmmaking & British Culture (London) program page

dayToDay.notes: Students stay 6 nights in gender-separated rooms in Imperia, Liguria, with Program Leaders on-site. The 5-day marine research course and the day-at-sea boat trip are supervised jointly by Rustic Pathways staff and the marine biologists of Delfini del Ponente, whose licensed commercial vessel has its own crew. Snorkeling is close to shore, weather-dependent, and called off rather than pushed when conditions are wrong. Median staff ratio 4.37:1 org-wide (never exceeding 7:1), max 16 students. The one predictable communication gap is the full day at sea (roughly 11am-5pm).
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Mediterranean Marine Biology in Italy program page, Supervision & Safety and Communication FAQ sections

dayToDay.notes: Students spend 5 nights in communal ecovillage accommodation in Cloughjordan (simpler than a hotel, gender-separated, by design), 2 nights in Dublin, and 4 nights in Iceland, all with Program Leaders on-site. Cloughjordan is a rural village with mobile coverage and Wi-Fi but noticeably slower speeds than a city; Dublin connectivity is unrestricted. Median staff ratio 4.37:1 org-wide (never exceeding 7:1), max 16 students, capped separately per departure. Workshops and land work in the ecovillage are run by residents and staff, not Rustic Pathways leaders directly.
dayToDay.sourceCitation: Ireland & Iceland: Ecovillage to Glacier program page, Supervision & Safety and Communication FAQ sections
